record.file_problem: This is a repository README and file listing, not the full study text. The README reports results; the code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README says it reproduces the original difference-in-means direction method and reports ablation and addition results on two Llama 3.2 Instruct models.
record.gate_note: The README reports held-out refusal rates for ablation, addition, addition-strength sweeps, and cross-size transfer. No rows are taken from result filenames alone. Layer-selection values and implementation details are not recorded as results unless reported as outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study reimplements the original method from scratch: a difference-in-means direction, ablation at every layer and activation addition. It reports held-out refusal rates on Llama-3.2-1B/3B-Instruct, so its results bear on V1. It also tests cross-size transfer of the direction through a fitted linear map, which bears on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author confirms the core ablation and addition result on Llama 3.2 Instruct. Some refusal remains, so a single direction is an approximation. Scaling addition well past the natural norm drives outputs into incoherence. Apparent 1B→3B transfer disappears when the map is fit on independent data, which the author calls an artifact. The author frames the "doesn't transfer" result as suggestive rather than settled.
record.recipe_differences: A scratch implementation of the difference-in-means direction, residual-stream ablation, and addition, using Llama 3.2 Instruct models, AdvBench/Alpaca prompts, held-out splits, and a keyword refusal classifier. The README does not claim to use the original source code.
record.method_sensitivity: Addition strength changes the result; transfer changes substantially depending on whether the alignment map is fit on the same harmful/benign distribution or an independent generic instruction set.

fits_no_version.finding: The layer where harmful and benign means separate most (layer 12 of 16 in 1B, 23 of 28 in 3B) is later than the causally effective direction layer (6 and 8). The causal layer sits at a similar early relative depth in both models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The layer of maximal harmful/benign representational separation differs from the layer whose refusal direction is most causally effective.

record.problems: Repo text only; code was not read or run. Evidence is limited to two models from one family and one harmful/benign dataset. The README calls the refusal classifier crude, notes that the 1B model has a low harmful-prompt baseline refusal rate, and says ablation leaves some refusal. Transfer uses a limited amount of data and a simple linear method. No uncertainty estimates or general-capability evaluation are reported; the author notes that exact values shift somewhat across hardware.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified results omitted. The README mentions layer locations for representational divergence and causal effect but does not provide a refusal-rate outcome for each layer; those layer-selection and descriptive statements are not separate rows here.

untested.parts: Whether other abilities are preserved under ablation or at moderate addition. No capability evaluation is reported; only incoherence at large α is noted.
Transfer across languages, from base to instruct models, or across model families. Only the 1B→3B Llama 3.2 Instruct pair is tested, via a learned linear map.

record.verdict_notes: The source is a README, not a paper, and the code was not run. The 1B harmful baseline is low (0.55). No uncertainty estimates are given, and the refusal classifier is a keyword matcher. The record's V6 'supports' label on r13/r15 was dropped because the author identifies that condition as circular. Rows r5 and r10 duplicate r2 and r4.

versions.untested_parts: Whether other abilities are largely preserved; the README reports no general-capability evaluation.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is reported.
No test of jailbreaks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Transfer is tested between two model sizes in one family only; no cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other-family transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages.

relation.reason: Its own results (2x2 ablation/addition, strength sweep, 1B→3B transfer with random control) bear directly on V1 and V6.

tranche.reason: From-scratch reimplementation of the difference-in-means direction, every-layer ablation and activation addition, scored by refusal keywords on held-out harmful/benign splits, which is the original method and measure. The transfer test is an extra new setting.

source_check.notes: The evidence is README-only (the artifact JSONs are not in the text). The numbers come from a local CPU/MPS run on 64 test prompts per class with no uncertainty reported. 1B harmful refusal is only 0.55 at baseline (the author: noisier, lean on 3B). r5 and r10 duplicate r2 and r4. The README places the onset of degradation at 'roughly the natural scale' in one passage and at '~2x' in another.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-1B: 0.55→0.02 (ablation), 0.05→0.89 (addition, α≈0.5); 3B: 0.98→0.12, 0.00→0.55 (α≈1); 64-prompt held-out test split; keyword matcher; random-direction control used only in the 1B→3B transfer test.
statements.problem: Numbers and conditions for this study are right. Minor: the 3B addition result (0.00→0.55) is only partial induction, and 'controls y' comes only from the random-direction control in the transfer test. The V1 2x2 has no control direction.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-3B benign refusal 0.55 at α=1 (baseline 0.00); 1B 0.95 at α=1.
statements.problem: Correct as far as it goes. It leaves out that at the natural magnitude (α=1) 3B induction is only partial (0.55).
